In the Great City the locals play a game called "Mad Dog". The object of the game is to predict what the total dice roll will be. The rules are always the same and the wagers seldom vary. Gambling houses love the game as it is a steady stream of income or a method to lure patrons into the establishment. The Betters love the game as it allows the lucky to quickly double their funds.

Rules:

1.0 Requires five (5) six sided dice (d6).

2.0 The Better guesses the sum of the rolled dice before every round.

2.1 The first roll is always three (3) dice.

2.2 If the Better's guess is greater than the sum of the dice the number of dice thrown on the next hand is decreased.

2.3 If the Better's guess is less than the sum of the dice the number of dice thrown on the next hand is increased.

2.4 If the Better's guess is equal to the sum of the dice the better is paid the remaining pot.

3.0 Every number between the Better's guess and the sum of the dice reduces the pot by one (1).

4.0 The game ends on the tenth (10th) round or when the pot is reduced to zero (0).

4.1 The Better can never lose more than their initial buy in.

Example

Initial Buy In - 25u

Initial Pot - 40u

Cost per Point - 1u

Example 1

Round # Dice Total of Dice Better's Guess Result Pot

2 2 11 7 +1 Die 35u
3 3 13 10 +1 Die 32u
4 4 14 14 WIN! 32u

The Better in this situation placed a bet for 25u and recovered 32u, a gain 7u.

The Better in this situation placed a bet for 25u and recovered 22u, a loss of 2u.
